NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: A "vane-geometry reprofile" modification to the centrifugal pump impeller reduces cavitation erosion by flattening the local pressure gradient at the leading edge while operating at 85% best-efficiency flow. Standard practice uses a constant-thickness leading edge; our mitigation introduces a tapered-thickness profile that reduces local flow acceleration and pressure drop. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest practice is "cavitation-resistant coatings," which add material but do not alter the pressure-drop driving mechanism; our departure is in the geometry-induced pressure-gradient control. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by reducing the pressure gradient magnitude that drives vapor bubble formation and collapse near the vane leading edge.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the local pressure gradient ∇P ≈ ρv²/R, where ρ is fluid density, v is local velocity, and R is the local radius of curvature of the vane leading edge. By increasing the leading-edge radius of curvature (flattening the profile), the velocity gradient and thus pressure gradient are reduced. Magnitude verification: A 20% increase in leading-edge radius reduces ∇P by ≈36%, directly lowering the cavitation potential σ = (P-Pv)/(ρv²/2) and bubble collapse energy.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (a) Existing impeller material (stainless steel 316); (b) Standard CNC machining (replaces constant-thickness profile with tapered-thickness profile); (c) No additional instrumentation or control (geometry change is passive). The standard practice bill includes: (a) Impeller material; (b) CNC machining (constant profile); (c) Flow meter for operation. Our bill replaces only the machining step (b) with a different CNC program.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installation: Same (uses existing CNC machine); Commissioning: Same (uses existing flow meter, no new calibration); Operation: Same (no additional control); Maintenance: Same (no additional steps); Cost Class: Same (CNC machining cost unchanged). Total burden: Same as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install modified impeller in test loop; run at 85% best-efficiency flow with NPSH margin >1.5 m for 1000 hours. Instruments: Existing pressure transducers, flow meter, and erosion probes. Pass/fail: Erosion depth <0.1 mm at leading edge after 1000 hours (vs. 0.5 mm for standard impeller). Kill criterion: If erosion exceeds 0.15 mm at any point, test fails. Duration: 1000 hours (accelerated test). Falsification: If erosion depth matches or exceeds standard impeller, the intervention is falsified.
